step0.prompt: [stern] Prove you're not soft. [grimly] The dead are walking the old charter road again. Put down a dozen of them, and we'll talk.

step1.prompt: [grudgingly] Not bad. [thoughtful] I mean to forge a Warden's blade one last time, but my forge is cold and my stock is empty. [gruff] Sixteen iron ingots. Good ones.

step2.prompt: [low voice] [serious] The blade's ready, but it needs a purpose. There's a barrow where my old master was laid to rest... and something wearing his armour rules it now. [softly] Lay him to rest properly.

waiting.prompt: [impatient] [gruff] Standing around won't get it done. Off with you.

finale.prompt: [quietly] [moved] So it's done. He can rest. [clears throat] [gruff] Here, a Warden's blade is no use hanging on my wall. [solemn] The oath goes: 'The road is the only home we keep.' [gruff] Don't make me regret it.

done.prompt: [warmly] [gruff] The road is long, adventurer. Keep it clear.

topic.wardens.0.prompt: [proudly] [remembering] The best of the Old Guild. No village to call home, no crown, no coin worth counting. [softly] We walked the roads between the bells, and kept the beasts off the carts.

topic.wardens.1.prompt: [wistful] That's all it was. [pause] That was everything. [bitter] When the Wardens went, the roads went with them. [sighs] Look around you.

topic.halvard.0.prompt: [quietly, remembering] One, maybe. Halvard. Best sword I ever carried a shield for. When the King fell, Halvard stayed at his post... and they tell me he's standing there still.

topic.halvard.1.prompt: [dark] Dead men don't keep oaths. Something else is keeping his for him. [warning] If you ever meet him, don't stop to listen. Hit him, and keep hitting him. [sad] [softly] It's the only kindness left.

intro.prompt: [surprised] Oh! [excited] You're the one with the guild contracts, aren't you? Wren Ashdown, cartographer. [sheepish] Well, I will be, once I finish a map anyone believes.

step0.prompt: [eager] I'm charting where the Old Guild hid things. [sheepish] Problem is, I've drawn so many maps I've run out of paper. [conspiratorial] Bring me twelve sheets and I'll tell you what I'm really after.

step2.prompt: [nervous] Found the den. It goes deep, and something big lives at the bottom. [quickly] You go first. I'll take notes. [laughs nervously] Very brave notes.

finale.prompt: [excited] You found it! A real shard of the crown. [nervous] Seven of these together and the Hollow King wakes, so let's never put them together, yes? [warmly] Keep it. You'll mind it better than I would.

done.prompt: [determined] Six shards left out there. I'm marking every rumour on my map. [warmly] When you're ready, the world will be waiting.

topic.maps.0.prompt: [defensive] Every map I've ever sold was wrong. Not my fault! [exasperated] The villages stay put, but the roads wander off, and a map is mostly roads.

topic.maps.1.prompt: [dreamy] The Old Guild had perfect maps, apparently. Nobody's seen one in three hundred years. [proudly] So I'm drawing my own, and mine will be better, because mine will have notes in the margins.

topic.king.0.prompt: [storytelling] Everyone knows the song. A Warden so afraid of dying that he carved out his own heart and set a crown in its place. [sarcastic] Lovely bedtime story.

topic.king.1.prompt: [curious] The trouble is, the song stops too early. Something happened to that crown after they beat him, and nobody ever wrote down what. [mischievously] I have a theory. I always have a theory.

intro.prompt: [apologetic] Ah, forgive me, I didn't hear you come in. [softly] I'm Ilsa. I study the things most clerics pray never to hear of. [hushed] Chiefly, the Hollow King.

step0.prompt: [uneasy] The skeletons around here have started humming, all on the same note. [gently] Bring down ten of them and I'll listen to what's left.

step1.prompt: [worried] It's a summons. Something is calling the old court back together. [thoughtful] Amethyst holds a sound for a long time, so with eight shards I can catch the echo and learn where it comes from.

step2.prompt: [serious] The echo leads to a hollow where a crone keeps the King's old rites. She was one of his courtiers. [quietly] If she falls, the call goes quiet. [pause] For now.

waiting.prompt: [anxious] The bones are still humming. [softly] Please hurry, if you can.

finale.prompt: [relieved] The humming has stopped. [warmly] Thank you. I've copied out what I learned about the King and his court, and you should have it. [gently] And take this. I'd feel better knowing you carry it.

done.prompt: [thoughtful] The court is quiet, but quiet is not gone. [softly] I'll keep listening.

topic.bell.0.prompt: [earnest] My order rings a bell that makes no sound. [embarrassed] Please don't laugh. [gently] A bell can be heard without being loud, if you know how to listen.

topic.bell.1.prompt: [softly] The dead have very good ears. When we ring it, the restless ones lie down again. [pause] Usually. [troubled] The Hollow King's court has never once listened.

topic.court.0.prompt: [reciting] Six courtiers, each given a den to rule: the Broodmother, the Barrow Lord, the Drowned Herald, the Hollow Crone, the Frost Regent and the Ash Warden.

topic.court.1.prompt: [wry] I've read everything ever written about them. It isn't much, [dryly] and most of it was written by people who were running at the time.

pip.voice: James - Energetic, Charismatic, British Male Narrator (ElevenLabs voice library)

intro.prompt: [delighted] Ah! An adventurer! An actual one, with dents! [grandly] I'm Pip Larkspur, bard of the high roads, [sheepish] and I've sung the same three songs for a year. I need new material. [charming] You need someone to make you famous. We're perfect for each other.

step0.prompt: [dramatic] First, the small matter of my lute. [indignant] Some brute sat on it and every string snapped. [pleading] A dozen strings, please. Spider silk if you can, they're the only ones that hold a tune.

step1.prompt: [theatrical] Now, a ballad needs a monster. [ominous] Something green, silent and horribly sudden. [cheerful] Go and blow up, [catches himself] ah, no, stop half a dozen creepers, and remember what it felt like. [eager] I'll need details.

step2.prompt: [grandly] Every great ballad ends in a barrow. There's a dead lord in one out past the hills, and no one's ever written a verse about him that wasn't a lament. [passionate] Give me a triumph instead.

waiting.prompt: [exasperated] The song can't finish itself! [shooing] Off you go, and do something worth rhyming.

finale.prompt: [triumphant] There it is. Strings, a monster, and a barrow. That's a ballad! [excited] Here, I wrote it all down, every deed you've done. I'll sing it in every tavern from here to the coast. [warmly] Come back when you've done something new and I'll write you another verse.

done.prompt: [cheerful] Back for another verse? [playful] Do something worth singing about, and I'll be here.

topic.songs.0.prompt: [proudly] Three! The one about the miller's daughter, [pause] the one about the other miller's daughter, [pause] and the one about the goat.

topic.songs.1.prompt: [proudly] The goat one is my finest work. [wincing] Audiences disagree, loudly, and sometimes with vegetables. [sheepish] Which is why I need you.

topic.fame.0.prompt: [conspiratorial] Here's how fame works. You do something brave. I make it rhyme. A hundred taverns sing it, [knowing] and in ten years nobody remembers what really happened, only the song.

topic.fame.1.prompt: [cheerful] So you do the brave part, and leave the truth to me. Everybody wins. [smug] Especially me.

maren.voice: Beatrice - Mature Female Storyteller (ElevenLabs voice library)

scene0.p0.prompt: [calm] [hollow] Don't reach for your sword. I'm not one of his.

scene0.p1.prompt: [weary] My name is Maren. The old ledgers call me the Last Warden. [solemn] I tore the last page out of the Ledger of Names so the King could never read the names of those who broke him, and that page has kept me here ever since. [whispers] Not alive. Not gone.

scene0.p2.prompt: [grave] You carry three shards of his crown. Every one you take weakens his court, [warning] but it wakes him a little more too. [solemn] The shards can only be broken where he was crowned: the Hollow Throne.

scene0.p3.prompt: [resolute] Find all seven. When you have them, I'll be waiting at the throne, and we'll finish what my Wardens started.

scene1.p0.prompt: [relieved] [softly] You came. All seven. I can feel them from here.

scene1.p1.prompt: [urgent] When you set them on the Shattering Stone, he'll rise to take them back. He'll call his knights and the echoes of every courtier you've killed, [grim] and when the crown starts to burn, so will the sky.

scene1.p2.prompt: [weary] I can't hold a sword anymore, but I can still draw a bow. [commanding] Stand your ground and break his crown.

scene2.p0.prompt: [exhausted] [relieved] It's done. The crown is dust, [softly] and the page is finally quiet.

scene2.p1.prompt: [warmly] Your name is written on it now, under mine. [solemn] Keep the roads, Warden. [softly] The road is the only home we keep.

topic.oath.0.prompt: [softly] The road is the only home we keep. [wistful] That's the line everyone remembers.

topic.oath.1.prompt: [reciting] The rest goes: and when the road is dark, we are the light upon it, and when the light goes out, we are the road. [wistful] We were very young when we wrote it. [quietly] We meant every word.

idris.voice: Alistair - Cultured and Articulate (ElevenLabs voice library)

intro.prompt: [dry] Mind the lecterns, they're older than the city. [formal] I am Idris Vael, Magister of the Starwatch. We read the sky, we keep the old sorceries, [troubled] and lately we've been reading things in the sky I would rather not.

step0.prompt: [measured] If you'd study with us, show me you can bend the weave. I've loosed five ward-lights over the plaza. Put them out, and with sorcery, mind. [dry] A blade passes straight through them.

step1.prompt: [approving] Clean work. Welcome to the Starwatch, Candle. [wry] Now, our star charts are written in ink ground from lapis, and the last of ours went into a very long footnote. Two dozen pieces, if you would.

step2.prompt: [exasperated] The phantoms have taken to circling the city by night, and you cannot chart a sky that keeps flapping. [brisk] Bring down half a dozen, Lamp, and we can see again.

step3.prompt: [grave] A hedge-witch has our star-glass, the lens we read the omens through. She took it from a careless Lamp and fled to a hollow in the wilds. [warning] Fetch it back, Lantern. She has had time to prepare.

step4.prompt: [low, troubled] Through the glass I've seen who sent her. Silvan Marrow. He was a Beacon of this order before he learned to read the forbidden chart, the one that shows where the stars go out. [heavy] He waits at the old observatory. End it, Beacon. [softly] Gently, if he lets you.

waiting.prompt: [dry] The stars will wait. I, unfortunately, am less patient. Off you go.

finale.prompt: [hushed] The chart. And Silvan... [quickly] no, don't tell me. [proudly] The Starwatch names you a Star, the first in thirty years. [warmly] This staff was made for the last one. It has sat on a shelf waiting for someone who earned it.

done.prompt: [warmly] Back again? Look up tonight, Star, and tell me what you see.

work.prompt: [mildly] There is always work in a library. Have a look at this.

woken.prompt: [drowsy] Mm? Ah. [dry] The stars keep late hours, and so, it seems, do you.

topic.starwatch.0.prompt: [proudly] We watch. Every night for four hundred years, a Star or a Beacon has sat at the top of this city and written down the sky. The sorceries came later. [reflective] You learn a great deal about light, looking at it that long.

topic.starwatch.1.prompt: [wry] These days we teach whoever has the patience. The patience is rarer than the gift.

topic.omens.0.prompt: [grave] Stars going out. Not falling, not fading: going out, one by one, in the north, [quietly] where the old King's throne stands empty.

topic.omens.1.prompt: [uneasy] Something is drinking the light. [quietly] When I find out what, I would very much like to be wrong.

corra.voice: Cate - Cinematic British RP Narrator (ElevenLabs voice library)

intro.prompt: [appraising] You've the look of someone who holds a sword the right way round. [firm] I'm Corra Wystan, Knight-Commander of the Hearthsworn. We keep the Wardfires lit and the dead off the roads. [stern] The Order always needs hands, but it doesn't take them on faith.

step0.prompt: [brisk] Step into a ring with one of my knights. A spar, nothing more: the first to give ground yields. [challenging] Show me you can take a blow and give one back.

step1.prompt: [approving] You held. [solemn] Kneel... and rise, Squire of the Hearthsworn. [firm] Your first duty is the oldest one. Hollow soldiers walk the roads out of this city. Put ten of them back in the ground.

step2.prompt: [serious] There's a Wardfire on the road out of the city that the Hollow have gone for three nights running. Tonight it's yours. [firm] Hold it till dawn, Sworn. [grave] If it goes out, a whole road goes dark.

step3.prompt: [disgusted] A thieves' ring that calls itself the Quiet Hand meets somewhere in this city, under our noses. [cold] The Widow who runs it keeps a ledger of every guard she has ever bought. [firm] Bring me that ledger, Knight.

step4.prompt: [grave] The Order has hunted the Dusk Rider for a hundred years. Every Banneret before you rode out to meet it, and every one came back on a shield. [quietly] I wouldn't ask if I thought anyone else could do it. [resolute] Bring the Rider down.

waiting.prompt: [stern] The dead don't rest because we do. On your way, and come back with it done.

finale.prompt: [stunned] It's over. A hundred years, and it's over. [moved] You've earned a title no one has held since my mother's day: Hearthwarden. [solemn] And this. Hearthbrand was forged in the first Wardfire. It burns for those who keep the oath.

done.prompt: [warmly] Hearthwarden. The fires burn a little brighter with you on the road.

work.prompt: [brisk] There's always a road that needs clearing. Here.

woken.prompt: [startled] Hm? [gruff] I'm awake. I'm always awake. What is it?

rival.prompt: [cool] One more thing. Word is you've been seen with the Widow's people. I'll not ask. [warning] But bring me that ledger and they'll know who did it, and they'll never have you back.

expelled.prompt: [furious] You stole the Ember from this house. Get out of my sight. [cold] The Hearthsworn have nothing for you, now or ever.

topic.oath.0.prompt: [reciting] Keep the fire. Keep the road. Keep faith with those who sleep. [warmly] Three lines, and we spend our lives learning them.

topic.oath.1.prompt: [wry] Most knights swear to a lord. We swear to a campfire. [serious] People laugh, until it's the only light for twenty miles.

topic.wardens.0.prompt: [firm] No. The Wardens were something else: road-walkers, no home, no lord. [respectful] When they fell, the Order took up what it could. Their fires. Their roads. Not their name. [quietly] We hadn't earned it.

topic.wardens.1.prompt: [wistful] If you ever meet one, a real one, I'd give a great deal to shake their hand.

intro.prompt: [drily] Close the hatch, dear, there's a draught. [amused] You'll have heard of me, or you wouldn't have climbed all those stairs. Odile Fenn. Some call me the Widow, though I've never married. [wry] It discourages suitors. [smooth] We are the Quiet Hand, and we only take from those who will never miss it.

step0.prompt: [businesslike] Light fingers first, then we talk. Lift three purses off the nobles walking this city, and don't let them see you do it. [conspiratorial] Come at them from behind, crouch low, and be quick about it.

step1.prompt: [pleased] Not bad at all. Welcome to the Hand, Lookout. [conspiratorial] Now, House Varn keeps a ledger of debts in their manor in the noble quarter, and a great many people would sleep easier if it went missing. Walk in, take it, walk out. [amused] Their guards are poorly paid and bored. Don't let them stop being bored.

step2.prompt: [annoyed] Some cutthroat crew is robbing caravans on the roads out of the city, and they're not ours. [cold] Robbing travellers is bad for business, Cutpurse. Our business. Thin them out.

step3.prompt: [delighted] Now a real job. The Hearthsworn keep a relic in their chapter house, the Ember of the First Hearth, in a little gold box. I have a buyer who'll pay more for that box than the knights earn in a lifetime. [warning] Knights are sharper than house guards, Picklock. Mind them.

step4.prompt: [hushed, intense] This is the one I've waited thirty years for. The Regent keeps the Crown's own seal in the palace vault. With it I can write any order in the city. [smooth] Bring me the seal, Shadow, and you'll never need to steal again. [amused] Not that you'll stop.

waiting.prompt: [drily] Still here? A job doesn't do itself, dear. Not even ours.

finale.prompt: [breathless] The Regent's seal. Oh, that is beautiful. [warmly] You've done what I never could, my dear. [softly] The Hand has had a Right Hand only once before, and she's the reason I wear black. This was hers. Widow's Kiss. [gently] Use it kindly.

done.prompt: [warmly] My Right Hand. Sit, have a drink. [playful] Steal something on your way out, it keeps you in practice.

work.prompt: [smooth] Always something for clever hands. Here.

woken.prompt: [sleepy] Mm, at this hour? [amused] You're either very brave or very drunk. Sit.

rival.prompt: [knowing] You wear the knights' colours, don't you? Under the coat, where you think no one sees. [cool] Take this job and they'll know it was you. The Order doesn't forgive. [sweetly menacing] Neither do I, as it happens. I just smile more.

expelled.prompt: [cold fury] You brought the knights my ledger. Do you know how many people that ledger was keeping safe? [icy] Go. And don't ever climb these stairs again.

topic.hand.0.prompt: [fond] A family, of sorts. Cutpurses, picklocks, a forger, two very good liars. [amused] Every city has a thieves' ring. This city has a polite one.

topic.hand.1.prompt: [firm] We have rules. Nobody who can't spare it. Nobody hurt who doesn't deserve it. [cold] And nobody, ever, talks to the knights.

topic.widow.0.prompt: [drily] Black is a practical colour. It doesn't show dirt, it doesn't show blood, [amused] and men stop asking you to dance.

topic.widow.1.prompt: [softly] And I did lose someone, once. The best thief this city ever had. [fond] She stole the moon off the bottom of a well, or so she told it. [quietly] I keep her knife. One day I will give it away.

meet.prompt: [gruff, friendly] Evening. They say you pay on time. Mind if I share your fire?

intro.prompt: [dry] Bram Hale, late of the Greyhart Company. [grim] Late being the word that matters. [wry] I've a good sword arm, a bad knee and no master, and you look like someone who could use the first and put up with the second. [plain] Honest work for honest pay, and I'll walk with you.

join.prompt: [gruff] Aye, done. Lead on. [wry] I'll watch your back, you watch the pay.

decline.prompt: [unbothered] Fair enough. I've sat by worse fires. Come and find me when you want a sword.

hello.1.prompt: [dry] Go on. I'm listening. It's not as if I've anywhere better to be.

follow.prompt: [grunts] Aye. I'll walk where I can see your back.

wait.prompt: [gruff] I'll hold here. Don't be long. [grumbling] Standing still makes my knee talk.

step0.prompt: [low, serious] There are raiders on these roads, and I know whose colours they ride under. [bitter] Harl Voss, my old captain. Put down eight of his riders and I'll tell you what he did to earn it. [gruff] I don't ask favours often, so take it as meant.

step1.prompt: [low] Those riders have a camp, and it's Harl's. [contemptuous] Walls, watchfires, the whole proud mess, and the Greyhart pay chest in there somewhere, if he hasn't drunk it dry. step2.prompt: [subdued] Harl's dead, and I find I'm not glad, which surprises me. [steady] One debt left. Where the Greyharts fell there's a Hill Troll camp now, and our colours hang in it like washing. [firm] Bring a troll down, and bring the colours home.

waiting.prompt: [dry] Not done yet? I've waited longer for worse. Take your time, but not all of it.

step0.done.prompt: [grim] Eight. Good. I said I'd tell you what he'd done. [bitter, low] He led the Greyharts into a troll valley and rode off with the pay chest while we were busy dying. [quiet] Sixty good men.

step1.done.prompt: [hollow] It's done. He knew me at the end. Looked right at me and said my name like it was a joke. [sighs] I'd hoped it would feel like more than this.

gated.prompt: [gruff] Not yet. Ask me again when we've shared a few more fires.

finale.prompt: [moved, quiet] The colours, home at last. [gruff] Take this, with my thanks. It was Harl's sword once, and I had the smith hammer the lie out of it and put the hart on the blade where it belongs. [proud, warm] There's one Greyhart left, and he stands where you stand.

done.prompt: [warm] Shield-brother. [gruff] Where to, and who's paying?

standing.0.prompt: [cold] Cold. You've done nothing to earn my trust, and a thing or two to lose it. [dry] Mind you, pay is still pay.

standing.1.prompt: [guarded] Wary. Not bad, not good. [dry] I've worked for worse, and I've watched them hang.

standing.2.prompt: [grudging] Better than it was. You pay what you say, and you don't flinch. That's two more than most.

standing.3.prompt: [sincere] I'd stand at your shoulder in a bad spot, and I don't say that to many. [gruff] Don't make a liar of me.

standing.4.prompt: [warm] Near enough sworn, if you want it said. [chuckles] I'd walk into a troll's kitchen for you, and I've done worse for less.

standing.5.prompt: [proud] Sworn. Shield-brothers, you and I. [quiet, warm] The Greyharts would have had you, and that's the best thing I know how to say.

gift.prompt: [pleased] Now that's a gift a man can use. [gruff] Thank you. I'll not make a speech of it.

gift_again.prompt: [amused] You've fed me once already today. Any more and I'll get ideas, or fat.

topic.greyharts.0.prompt: [fond] Sixty swords and a grey hart on the banner. We took honest contracts, kept to them, and never left a village worse than we found it. That was the whole creed, and a decent one.

topic.greyharts.1.prompt: [darker] It ended in a valley, under a captain I'd have followed anywhere. [bitter] That's the trouble with that kind of captain. [gruff] Ask me about him when I've had a drink.

topic.coin.0.prompt: [dry] Because a Guild Mark in the hand is the only promise I've ever seen kept. I've been paid in thanks, in glory and in fine speeches, [wry] and I've never once eaten a speech.

topic.coin.1.prompt: [matter-of-fact] A contract's the same. Two names, a price, a day it's done. [hard] Break one with me and we're finished. [softer] Keep it, and I'd walk through a wall for you. It's simple, which is why I like it.

leave.prompt: [angry, low] I've been sold out once, and I'll not stand and watch it happen twice. I'm done. Keep your road.

cold.prompt: [curt] Not today. Give me time to cool, and a drink to help.

return.prompt: [gruff] I thought it over, with a tankard's help. [grudging] You're not good company yet, but I've had worse. Lead on.

bark.approve.fight.prompt: [laughs] Ha. Now that was a proper fight.

bark.approve.help.prompt: [approving] Honest work, honestly done. I like that.

bark.disapprove.theft.prompt: [disappointed] Thieving from honest folk? I'd hoped you were better than that.

bark.disapprove.murder.prompt: [cold, low] You killed someone who couldn't fight back. I'll not forget it.

bark.faction.hearthsworn.prompt: [approving] The Hearthsworn. They keep the fires lit. Well chosen.

bark.faction.quiet_hand.prompt: [scornful] The Quiet Hand. Thieves with manners are still thieves.

bark.ask.prompt: [hesitant] A word, when you've a moment. I've a favour to ask.

bark.camp.0.prompt: [fond, amused] First contract I ever took with the Greyharts was a wedding. Sixty swords to guard one bride, and the groom's mother sent the lot of us to the kitchen for being underfoot. [chuckles] Best fed we ever were.

bark.camp.2.prompt: [quiet, haunted] Sixty of us stood in that valley, and fifty-nine had the decency to die. I lay under the colours and the trolls took me for dead, and I let them. [ashamed] I've never forgiven myself for being good at it.

bark.region.prompt: [wary] New country. Don't trust it yet.

bark.capital.prompt: [dry] Fine walls. I'd wager the prices are finer. Mind your purse.

bark.night.prompt: [gruff] Light's going. Time we found a fire.

bark.rain.prompt: [grumbling] Rain. My knee told me an hour ago.

bark.deep.prompt: [uneasy] Too much rock over my head. I don't like it.

bark.hurt.prompt: [urgent] You're bleeding badly. Fall back and drink something. Now.

bark.boss.prompt: [grim relish] That's a big one. Good. Big ones fall loudest.

bark.victory.prompt: [breathing hard] Still standing. That counts as a win.

bark.downed.prompt: [pained] Down, but not out. Give me a moment.

bark.revived.prompt: [groans] Obliged. Don't tell anyone I needed it.

bark.respawn.prompt: [dry] Back from the dead. Try not to make a habit of it.

bark.idle.0.prompt: [dry] I've slept in worse places than this. Not many, mind.

bark.idle.1.prompt: [grumbling] No decent pint in a week. I'm not complaining. I'm noting it.

bark.idle.2.prompt: [wry] A man who says money isn't everything has always got some.

bark.swap.prompt: [sour] Someone else, is it? Fine. I'll wait here until their sword breaks.

intro.prompt: [cocky] Kestrel Vey, ranger of the Thornwood, [smirking] which is what poachers call themselves once they've got a decent bow. [confident] Take me along and nothing sneaks up on you. [beat, wry] Probably.

bark.idle.1.prompt: [inhales, content] Smell that? Woodsmoke and wet leaves. Best smell there is.

bark.idle.2.prompt: [offhand, a little shy] I used to hate company. [quick] Don't let that go to your head.

[warm, self-deprecating] I pray, I heal, and I trip over my own hem, [light laugh] though I am much better at the first two. wait.prompt: [warm] I'll keep the place for you. [softly] Don't be long, and light keep you.

[hushed] There is a Warden's Watch where the Fallen Warden still keeps his post, and he is not at peace. [brave but afraid] I would go down to him, but not alone. [pleading softly] Will you help me give him rest?

waiting.prompt: [patient] Take the time you need, friend. [gently urgent] But not too much, if you can. The dead aren't resting.

step0.done.prompt: [peaceful, grateful] Eight at rest. Thank you, friend. I said the words over every one, and I think the roads breathe easier. [relieved sigh] So do I.

step1.done.prompt: [awed, joyful] Three fires, burning again. Can you see them from here? [emotional] That is what we were for. [softly] Thank you for helping me remember.

gated.prompt: [apologetic, kind] Not yet, friend. Ask me again when we have walked a little further together.

finale.prompt: [hushed, reverent] He is at rest. I felt it go quiet, like a bell that has finished ringing. Whatever falls on you, I will be there with the light.

done.prompt: [bright, warm] Light keep you, friend. Where shall we walk today?

standing.0.prompt: [gentle, hopeful] Like strangers at a fire that hasn't caught. It may yet. [softly] I would like it to.

standing.1.prompt: [thoughtful] Carefully, I think. I'm still deciding about you, and you about me. [kind] That's allowed.

standing.2.prompt: [warm] Better. The fire has caught, and I'm glad of your company, whatever else is true.

standing.3.prompt: [sincere] I trust you, friend. I would put my life in your hands and my prayers at your back, [earnest] and I do not say that lightly.

standing.4.prompt: [fond] Close as kin, nearly. [smiling] A step or two more and I'll call you sworn, and mean it.

standing.5.prompt: [solemn, joyful] Sworn. By light, by road, and by every fire we've kindled. [tender] There is nothing between us now but the road.

topic.lamplighters.0.prompt: [fond, reminiscing] A small order, never more than a score of us along all the roads. Every Wardfire had one of us to tend it. Trim the wick, say the words, keep the dark honest. [quiet pride] Nobody sang about us. We kept the lights on.

topic.shrine.0.prompt: [soft, remembering] It stood on the marsh road, a little house of reed and brick with a lamp in every window. Seven sisters, and me. [quiet, pained] I was away on pilgrimage when the Hollow came.

leave.prompt: [sorrowful, firm] I'm sorry, friend. Truly. I cannot walk this road with you any longer. I've prayed on it, and the light says no. [sad, gentle] May it keep you better than I could.

return.prompt: [tentative, hopeful] I prayed on it, and the light said you were worth one more try. [pleading] Please don't make me regret it.

bark.approve.fight.prompt: [relieved, admiring] Light be thanked. That was bravely done.

bark.approve.help.prompt: [warm] Good work, friend. The roads are lighter for it.

bark.ask.prompt: [timid] A moment, friend, when you can? I've something to ask.

bark.camp.2.prompt: [hushed, sad] I light seven candles each night, one for every sister. It doesn't help, but it doesn't hurt either. [fragile] Some nights I count them twice, in case I've missed one. [barely a whisper] I never have.

bark.region.prompt: [curious, gentle] A new land. I wonder whose fire we'll find in it.

bark.capital.prompt: [amazed] So many lamps! [giggles] Whoever lights these every night must be exhausted.

bark.night.prompt: [gentle] Dusk, friend. Let's find a fire before the dark finds us.

bark.deep.prompt: [nervous] I don't like it down here. So much dark, and no sky.

meet.prompt: [nervous, rushed] Hello, sorry. I heard you know sorcery. May I sit? [awkward laugh] I talk when nervous.

bark.idle.2.prompt: [anxious, musing] I wonder if anyone's reading my notebook right now. [quick] Don't answer that.
